newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block cuts qtrly div to $0.20 a share.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block cuts qtrly div to $0.20 a share.

text.p: H&R Block Inc said on Thursday that its directors voted to cut the company's quarterly cash dividend payment to $0.20 a share from $0.32.
H&R Block said its board had indicated last July that it would reduce its dividend following the separation of the company's CompuServe Corp operations.
The dividend is payable January 2, 1997, to shareholders of record December 12, 1996.

"Even though the separation has not been completed, the board decided such action was prudent at this time because CompuServe is not adding to the company's profitability," said Frank Salizzoni, H&R Block's president and chief executive officer and CompuServe's chairman.
"In taking this action today, the board is indicating it anticipates the separation of CompuServe," he said in a statement. H&R Block holds 80.1 percent of CompuServe.
On an annualized basis, the new dividend is based on the company's earnings from tax and financial operations as well as its historical payout ratio, Salizzoni said.
Earlier today, H&R Block reported a loss for its fiscal second quarter ended October 31, 1996 of $74.1 million or $0.71 a share.
H&R Block said its loss was primarily due to CompuServe's fiscal second quarter loss of $58 million or $0.63 a share. H&R Block's share of CompuServe's loss was $46.5 million or $0.45 a share.
